ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18969, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act; Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended); Korea FIU AML/CFT regulations implementing FATF Recommendations, jointly enforced by the National Tax Service, district courts and the Financial Supervisory Service.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registrar or companies registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize locally if required, then obtain an Apostille from the origin state's competent authority only if the origin state is a Hague Apostille Convention member; if the origin state is a non-member, complete Korean consulate or embassy consular legalization instead. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel paths and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registrar or a certified chamber of commerce in the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize locally if required, then obtain an Apostille from the origin state's competent authority if the origin state is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise, Korean consular legalization via the Korean Embassy or Consulate with jurisdiction. Do not combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the Korean incorporation and UBO filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or authorized representative of each foreign corporate shareholder, notarized by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If shareholder's jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, attach an Apostille to the notarized resolution issued by the relevant state competent authority; if a non-member, use Korean consular legalization. These paths are mutually exclusive and sequential combination is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jeong-gwan) of the Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and the promoters of the Korean entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public is required for domestic incorporation; if the Articles must be used in a foreign jurisdiction, obtain an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. No Korean consular legalization is applied inside Korea.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for each participant or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of the shareholder or beneficial owner, issued on bank letterhead and signed by an authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-issue letter must be notarized and then Apostillized by the signatory state's competent authority if the signatory state belongs to the Apostille Convention; if not, Korean consular legalization at the local Korean diplomatic mission. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative routes and cannot be merged.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, each shareholder, promoter, director, officer, ultimate beneficial owner and authorized signatory must be screened against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit's AML checklists, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, United Kingdom and European Union consolidated sanctions lists, Korean government asset-freeze notices and reputable commercial adverse-media databases. The screening must include foreign and domestic politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates, with enhanced due diligence for high-risk jurisdictions, source-of-wealth verification, adverse-media review and a live transaction-monitoring trigger for the first five years after account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: IROS (Internet Registration System of the Supreme Court of Korea) / local District Court Registry Office business name search service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must include a Korean Hangul component representing the distinguishing name, followed by the business scope words and the legal form suffix Chusik Hoesa (or Jusik Hoesa). Foreign-language words are admitted only as supplementary transliteration or acronyms, and the four-tier naming convention requires: (1) distinctive Korean word or transliteration, (2) genuine business-purpose descriptor, (3) permissible separator or symbol, and (4) mandatory legal form suffix. A name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered Korean mark or company name is prohibited.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must first obtain the written rejection reason from the competent registry clerk or the IROS system. Within 30 days of rejection, the applicant should file a written objection with the same registry asking for reconsideration, then an administrative appeal to the relevant District Court if reconsideration fails, or an application to the Administrative Court under the Administrative Litigation Act. The appeal must contain the proposed corrected name, a legal argument distinguishing the prior mark or name, and evidence of the claimant's legitimate business purpose, and should be filed through an attorney to preserve statutory time limits.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the sole registered address for a Korean Chusik Hoesa engaged in cross-border reverse logistics. Under the Commercial Act, VAT Act and the registration supervision rules, a physical operational address in Korea is mandatory. Local tax offices and banks uniformly reject mail-only addresses for this industry because returns, quality grading and RMA operations require an actual warehouse, storage area or business site. A separate correspondence address may complement, not replace, the registered operational office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: moderate to high, approximately 30% probability within the first 12 months and rising to 50% if customs bonded operations or large value returns are declared. The inspector will check: lease agreement or title deed; utility bills; external signage matching the registered name; physical presence of employees; inventory and return-merchandise storage; sorting equipment; RMA reconciliation records; tax invoices and warehouse logs. Failure to pass an unannounced inspection may result in business registration cancellation, tax penalties and bank account restrictions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, as amended, particularly Articles 288, 289, 292, 295, 300, 312, 313, 317, 329, 383, 388, 390, 409 and 412; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 2, 4, 5 and 8; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Value-Added Tax Act Article 8; and applicable registration fee schedules of the Supreme Court and local tax ordinances.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Company Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, filed through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS); post-formation business registration is completed at the National Tax Service via HomeTax.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation, supported by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital subscription deposit certificate, minutes of the incorporation meeting, officer acceptance statements and foreign investment notification certificate where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the Hometax electronic web portal at hometax.go.kr for registration, electronic tax invoices, and declarations; customs-side export controls are handled by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign non-resident founders establishing the Korean Chusik Hoesa must first create a domestic business place in Korea for the entity, then file a business registration application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the Korean address. The filing set comprises the foreign parent or founder's certificate of incorporation and foreign registration certificate, Korean or English notarized and apostilled translations, the Korean entity's articles of incorporation, director identification, power of attorney for the local fiscal representative, proof of lease or ownership of the domestic place of business, and a bank account certificate for the Korean entity's foreign-currency receipts. Once NTS accepts the application, the entity receives a single ten-digit Business Registration Number that serves simultaneously as the Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number, the VAT registration number, and the withholding agent number. Foreign non-resident digital suppliers that have no Korean fixed establishment may, in limited cases, use the streamlined Hometax foreign non-resident registration path; however, for this reverse-logistics operation the ordinary domestic business registration path is mandatory, and any subsequent address or representative changes must be updated through Hometax within the statutory filing deadlines.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Chusik Hoesa cannot elect pass-through treatment; Korean corporate income tax is levied at the entity level. A qualifying controlling resident corporation may, however, elect consolidated corporate income tax filing with its wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries under the Corporate Tax Act, and affiliated businesses may apply to the NTS for VAT group registration; neither election alters the entity-level classification of this Corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) administered by the National Tax Service under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no monetary de minimis threshold for a stock corporation; the Chusik Hoesa is required to be VAT-registered from the commencement of any taxable business activity in Korea. A simplified taxpayer regime covers only certain individually-operated micro-businesses with annual taxable revenue below KRW 80,000,000, and it is not available to ordinary corporations; therefore this entity must obtain full VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A registered business with VAT taxable turnover exceeding KRW 80,000,000 must issue, through the Hometax e-Tax Invoice System or an NTS-approved electronic data interchange or API service provider, an electronic tax invoice for each taxable supply. The e-invoice data is transmitted to the NTS no later than the day following the tax invoice issue date; the NTS performs real-time format validation and assigns a unique electronic approval number, thereby creating a digital audit trail. No separate anti-fraud fiscal stamp is imposed, but the NTS system automatically compares e-invoice issuance with the filed VAT return and can pre-flag unexplained discrepancies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods supplied by the Korean entity to a foreign buyer are zero-rated when the Korea Customs Service accepts an export declaration and the goods legally leave Korea, provided the exporter receives the foreign-currency sales proceeds within 180 days. Cross-border reverse logistics and returned-goods quality-grading services supplied for a foreign principal or an offshore e-commerce seller are zero-rated as foreign-currency-earning services when the recipient is a non-resident, the services are used outside Korea, the services are separately invoiced to the non-resident counterparty, and the consideration is repatriated to Korea in foreign currency as evidenced by a foreign exchange receipt certificate. In both cases the zero-rating fails if the substantiating documentation is incomplete, inconsistent, or involves circular fund flows through affiliated accounts without actual cross-border foreign exchange.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service accepted outbound export declaration (Export Bill of Entry) with export declaration number from UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) showing the actual shipment leaving Korean customs territory
Commercial invoice, packing list, container number, and weight manifest matching the export declaration

Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate (Certificate of Issuance of Foreign Exchange) issued by an authorized foreign-exchange bank in Korea, or a bank ledger and SWIFT MT103 evidence proving inward foreign-currency remittance
Executed international sales contract or service purchase order identifying the foreign buyer or principal, freight terms, return-merchandise quality-grading service scope, and payment currency
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice issued to the foreign buyer, internal reverse-logistics work orders, and inspection-grade reports evidencing actual performance of the ISIC 5229 services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may disallow the 0% rate and retroactively assess VAT at the standard 10% rate on the unsubstantiated export, together with statutory additional taxes for under-reporting and non-issuance of electronic tax invoices, plus monthly late-payment surcharges. The statutory limitation period for VAT assessment is generally five years from the filing date, extended to ten years for cases involving fraudulent evasion or deliberately false documentation. Fraudulent or grossly negligent zero-rating claims are also subject to the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, which may impose criminal imprisonment of up to five years or a fine of not less than five times the evaded tax amount, in addition to civil penalties, forfeiture of offsetting input VAT, and disqualification of refund claims for the tax year.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) - the central foreign exchange regulator under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, coordinating with the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the Financial Supervisory Service, and the Korea Customs Service through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a notification-centred rather than permission-based foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is convertible for current account items such as trade settlements, service fees, refunds, and dividends, provided that an authorised foreign exchange bank obtains the underlying contract, invoice, customs declaration or certificate evidencing the payment. Capital account transactions, including an inbound capital contribution from a foreign shareholder, are generally permitted but must be reported through FEIS and in some cases require a certificate of foreign investment from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy. Dividend remittance out of audited profits is recognised as a current account transfer and can be processed without a separate exchange licence, but banks will require board minutes, audited financial statements and tax clearance to demonstrate that withholding taxes have been settled. Macroprudential measures such as the leveraged FX derivative ceiling can temporarily tighten daily liquidity, yet they do not delay ordinary reverse logistics refund flows. For export-related receipts in reverse logistics, no mandatory surrender of foreign currency to the won is imposed; exporters may hold proceeds in resident foreign currency accounts at domestic banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, export proceeds for goods must be collected within one year from the actual export date, while service-related proceeds are generally collected within one year from service completion. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio; the exporter may retain foreign currency in a resident foreign currency deposit account at an authorised Korean bank or convert to KRW at the prevailing market rate. If converted, the bank must report the transaction to FEIS using the underlying contract or invoice. Extension of the collection period can be obtained for delayed receivables caused by long-term construction, shipping disputes, overseas claims, or other justification approved by the foreign exchange bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary account. Offshore digital EMIs such as Airwallex are not authorised by the Korean Banking Act to hold corporate deposit accounts or act as clearing institutions in South Korea. They are not domestic banks and cannot provide a statutory escrow, trade settlement, or FEIS reporting account. Offshore EMIs may connect to Korean banks through white-labelled local banking partners for execution of cross-border payments, but the operating entity must maintain a Tier-1 Korean bank account as the legal account for capital escrow, KRW operations, FX reporting, and trade settlement. For this reverse logistics Chusik Hoesa, Airwallex can be used only as a supplementary execution layer after the domestic banking relationship is fully established.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean real-name identification rules and FSS AML guidelines require representative directors and authorised signatories to be identified through an in-person interview or a live-video interview conducted under bank-controlled authentication procedures. For a non-resident director, full physical presence in the branch may be waived when the director appears before a Korean consular officer or a designated overseas branch of the same Korean bank, produces an apostilled power of attorney, and submits a notarised certificate of corporate existence and passport copy. Most Tier-1 banks will still require one statutory director with a Korean business registration number or a local representative with an original power of attorney to appear at the branch during account opening. Hybrid remote opening is accepted for low-risk corporate structures but documentary standards are strict and subject to the compliance committee review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identification blocker: layered foreign shareholders or nominee holdings obscure the ultimate controller of the Chusik Hoesa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korean corporate registry certificate issued by the court, full shareholder ledger, certified copies of overseas corporate registry certificates for all intermediate entities, notarised UBO declarations naming every individual with 25% or more direct or indirect ownership, ownership chain diagram with percentage controls, and a board resolution confirming no bearer shares or nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering flag: return-merchandise refunds and quality grading fees look like non-trade payments without verified physical goods movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed reverse logistics service and warehousing agreements, inbound and outbound customs declarations, airway bills or bills of lading with proof of delivery, warehouse receiving notes with condition and grading photographs, inspection and quality grading certificates, sequential refund reconciliation showing original order IDs with corresponding customer refund records, and carrier reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds uncertainty: non-resident shareholder capital injection raises tax transparency and money-laundering concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital escrow receipt or certificate of paid-in capital deposit issued by the Korean bank, audited or notarised financial statements of each investing entity, six-month bank statements from the remitting account, source-of-wealth statement with supporting asset documentation, signed investment or share subscription agreement, and the FEIS report confirming the remittance and purpose code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and adverse media exposure on foreign directors or beneficial owners with name matches or incomplete residential history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies and overseas proof of residence or Korean resident registration cards, sanctions-screening results against UN, EU, UK, OFAC and Korean government designations, PEP declarations for every director and UBO, negative-media search reports, notarised explanations for any name hits, and a completed enhanced due diligence questionnaire submitted to the bank compliance team.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders should remit equity capital via SWIFT from their corporate bank account to the Chusik Hoesa capital escrow or paid-in capital account at a Tier-1 Korean bank. The remittance message must clearly state the investment nature and the corresponding FEIS transaction purpose code. If the payment is in USD or another foreign currency, the Korean bank will execute the conversion to KRW at the market rate using the share subscription agreement or investment contract. The bank then issues a capital verification certificate which the company files with the court for incorporation or with the registry for a capital increase. If the structure qualifies as foreign investment, a report must be filed with KOTRA or the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and the subsequent foreign investment registration certificate should be retained in the bank file so that future dividend remittances and foreign exchange conversions are not blocked. All capital and service flows must be supported by the underlying reverse logistics commercial contract or order to avoid false-invoice classification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic merchant refunds and logistics vendor payments should be cleared through the KFTC local ACH rail using the company KRW current account. Cross-border supplier payments, refunds to overseas merchants, and quality-grading fees must be executed through SWIFT MT103 transmissions using the corresponding FEIS trade or service purpose code, supported by credit notes, inspection certificates, original order numbers, and customs declarations when goods physically cross the border. For large return consignments and restocking deliveries, a commercial letter of credit or documentary collection is recommended, with bill of lading, packing list, and inspection report attached. The bank will expect an internally generated reconciliation schedule matching outbound payments to actual reverse logistics events and may require standing instruction limits for repetitive refund disbursements to reduce false-positive screening friction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Underlying-backed deliverable forward contracts (USD/KRW) for recognised trade receivables and payables arising from reverse logistics service fees, freight costs and returned-goods settlements, with maturity aligned to the contractual collection period and subject to bank credit approval and FEIS reporting.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only as a hedging instrument where the entity has genuine KRW/USD trade exposure and the bank documents the underlying transaction; speculative NDF positions by a non-financial corporate treasury are not permitted under Korean FX regulations.

Foreign exchange swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps can be used only to hedge long-term foreign shareholder loans or investment payables, with a documented debt-service schedule, confirmed drawdown, and FSS reporting; speculative short-term swaps are not permitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular General Shareholders' Meeting and statutory approval of the annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing; the duly executed minutes and supporting financial statements must be retained at the registered office and produced upon shareholder or court request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after each fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the meeting must be convened by March 31 of the subsequent year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene without just cause permits any shareholder to petition the competent district court to authorize convocation; each defaulting director may be exposed to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,800) under the Korean Commercial Act; repeated failure to hold the meeting can otherwise impair corporate filings and trigger the dormant-corporation dissolution procedure under KCC Article 520-2.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: National corporate income tax return and tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, file and pay by March 31 of the following year; for special fiscal years, within 3 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled or non-reported taxable income attracts an additional tax of 20% of the unfiled tax amount; underreported income attracts 10% of the underreported tax amount; overdue taxes accrue daily delinquency interest of 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum); continued non-filing and non-payment can lead to asset seizure, compulsory collection, and judicial dissolution; sustained inactivity for 5 or more years may trigger the dormant-corporation administrative dissolution procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surcharge return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the registered place of business (Si / Gun / Gu) via the local tax integrated system (WeTax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, pay and file the local corporate income tax surcharge (10% of national corporate income tax) by March 31 of the following year, or within 10 days after the national corporate income tax filing due date when separately assessed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underreported or unfiled local corporate income tax incurs an additional local tax charge of 20% or 10% respectively, plus daily overdue interest of 0.022%; prolonged delinquency can trigger local compulsory collection, seizure of bank accounts and bonded assets, and court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax preliminary return for the first quarter (January 1 to March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File and pay by April 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or failure to adequately report triggers an additional VAT penalty of 20% of the unreported VAT, 10% for underreporting, and daily overdue interest of 0.022% per day on unpaid VAT; willful recurrent evasion can support criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax final return for the first half-year (April 1 to June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File and pay by July 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or failure to adequately report triggers an additional VAT penalty of 20% of the unreported VAT, 10% for underreporting, and daily overdue interest of 0.022% per day on unpaid VAT; willful recurrent evasion can support criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax preliminary return for the third quarter (July 1 to September 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File and pay by October 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or failure to adequately report triggers an additional VAT penalty of 20% of the unreported VAT, 10% for underreporting, and daily overdue interest of 0.022% per day on unpaid VAT; willful recurrent evasion can support criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax final return for the second half-year (October 1 to December 31) and annual aggregate settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File and pay by January 25 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or failure to adequately report triggers an additional VAT penalty of 20% of the unreported VAT, 10% for underreporting, and daily overdue interest of 0.022% per day on unpaid VAT; willful recurrent evasion can support criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report submission and audited financial statements lodgement (only if the statutory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system, and National Tax Service when audited financial statements must be attached to the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements and the independent audit report must be finalized before the regular shareholders' meeting; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the tax-attached audited financial statements and audit report are due with the corporate income tax return by March 31 of the following year, and the separate FSS/DART submission must be completed within the statutory period after the shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an independent CPA auditor, failure to obtain the audit report, or failure to submit audited financial statements may subject the company and its representatives to regulatory sanctions under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, including administrative fines, designation of an auditor by the Financial Services Commission, and adverse evidentiary consequences in tax disputes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual balance sheet public disclosure for a Chusik Hoesa with share capital of KRW 1 billion or more
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing; disclosure made through the company's website, the official gazette, or one or more daily newspapers as prescribed by the Korean Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks after the regular general shareholders' meeting at which the financial statements were approved
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish the balance sheet as required exposes the company to an administrative fine against the responsible directors and may impair creditworthiness and ability to obtain tax compliance certificates; persistent omission may be treated as a serious corporate governance violation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily subject to an independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit if its total assets as of the previous fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000). Companies whose securities are listed or traded on the Korea Exchange (KOSPI or KOSDAQ) are always subject to external audit regardless of asset size. A company may also be subject to a designated audit or compulsory external audit when ordered by the Financial Services Commission for public interest, credibility of accounting, or investor protection reasons. There is no independent headcount-based audit trigger under Korean law; the primary quantitative trigger is total assets, with secondary FSS designation powers for revenue and corporate-government-risk cases. A company that is not required to have an external audit may still be audited voluntarily, but the audited financial statements will be accepted only if prepared by a licensed accounting firm registered with the FSS.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Listed companies, financial institutions, and certain state-designated entities must apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS). Non-listed private stock corporations may apply K-IFRS or Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) as published by the Korean Accounting Standards Board. For small and medium entities, the Simplified Bookkeeping and K-SME GAAP may be used when eligibility requirements are met, but any entity subject to mandatory external audit must present financial statements in accordance with K-IFRS or K-GAAP, with a clear basis-of-preparation note and comparative figures. For tax filing purposes, financial statements must be reconciled to the taxable income calculation through the corporate income tax adjustment schedule.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A private Chusik Hoesa has no annual UBO return filed with the Korean court registry. However, the Register of Members is the legal source of shareholder title, and every transfer of shares must be recorded with the transferor's and transferee's names and titles in the register before the transfer can be asserted against the company. If a foreign investor directly or indirectly acquires or transfers shares, especially when the invested amount is at least KRW 100,000,000 or the ownership interest reaches or changes by 10% or more, the transaction must be reported through an authorized foreign exchange bank or to the competent authorities under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets, within 30 calendar days of the triggering transaction. For Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) purposes, the company must, upon opening or maintaining a bank account, identify and verify its beneficial owners; this information must be reconfirmed at least annually or whenever a material ownership change occurs. Any change in shares requiring the updating of the Register of Members must also be reflected in the directors' resolution minutes and, if the share capital structure changes, in the Commercial Registration Registry through a registration amendment filed with the competent district court within 2 weeks.
